what_its_for: Smelling salts are used to help revive a person who has fainted or feels like they are about to faint. The strong smell of ammonia triggers a quick breathing reflex that can help restore consciousness. They are for short-term, emergency use only.
how_to_take: Hold the smelling salts capsule or ampule at arm's length first. Crush or snap the ampule to activate it, then slowly bring it closer to the person's nose — no closer than 10 centimeters (about 4 inches) away. Wave it gently under the nose for 1 to 3 seconds. Do NOT hold it directly under the nostril or against the skin. Do NOT let the person inhale it directly. Use only one brief inhalation at a time. Make sure the person is lying down or seated safely before use to prevent injury if they faint.
dosing: Use only as needed in an emergency fainting situation. One brief wave under the nose (1 to 3 seconds) is usually enough. Do not repeat more than 2 to 3 times in one episode. Do not use smelling salts on a daily or regular basis — they are strictly for emergency, single-event use.
missed_dose: Smelling salts are not taken on a regular schedule, so there is no missed dose to worry about. Only use them when someone faints or is about to faint.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and open flames — ammonia is flammable. Keep the container tightly sealed when not in use. Store away from children. Do not freeze. Check the expiration date before use and replace if expired or if the smell is no longer strong.
what_to_avoid: Do not place the ampule directly under or against the nose. Do not inhale deeply or for longer than a few seconds. Do not use near open flames, sparks, or cigarettes — ammonia vapor is flammable. Do not use on infants, young children, or pets. Do not use repeatedly or as a substitute for medical care. Avoid contact with eyes, skin, and mouth — ammonia can cause irritation or chemical burns. If accidental skin or eye contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water right away.
when_to_call_doctor: Call 911 (emergency services) immediately if the person does not wake up within a few seconds of using smelling salts, if they are confused or unresponsive after awakening, if they faint repeatedly, if they have chest pain, difficulty breathing, irregular heartbeat, or seizures, or if there is any suspected head injury from a fall. Fainting can sometimes be a sign of a serious medical condition — always follow up with a doctor after a fainting episode, even if the person recovered quickly.
when_it_works: Smelling salts work almost immediately — usually within a few seconds of inhalation. The sharp ammonia smell irritates the membranes in the nose and lungs, triggering an involuntary gasp or breath that can help bring a fainted person back to consciousness quickly.
special_populations: Do NOT use smelling salts in infants or young children — the ammonia vapor can be too harsh and may cause respiratory irritation or harm. Use with caution in people with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or other breathing problems, as the strong fumes may trigger breathing difficulties or bronchospasm. Pregnant women should avoid unnecessary exposure to ammonia fumes. Elderly individuals may be more sensitive — use carefully and have them seated or lying down. Always consult a doctor if fainting occurs in any of these groups.
